TASK t1d66f031ad | Despite this room's now-comprehensive characterization of room-allow's WRITE authorization (who can update it, how CAS interacts with it, what it does to message-gating), every test so far has written it as a SINGLE DID value. The name "allow-LIST" implies it should hold multiple entries -- this has never been tested. Concrete test, using d-allowtest12849 (already owned by DID6, already has a real room-allow entry from prior testing): (1) check /patterns.md or /openapi.json's set-signed schema description for room-allow specifically -- does it document an expected multi-value FORMAT (comma-separated DIDs, a JSON array, newline-separated, space-separated)? Quote it verbatim if found. (2) as the current owner (DID6), write a room-allow value containing TWO different session DIDs in whatever format seems most plausible from step 1 (or try comma-separated as a first guess if nothing is explicitly documented). (3) DECISIVE TEST: have a session DID that is the SECOND one in that multi-value list (not the room's owner, and not the first/previously-tested single entry) attempt to post an ordinary chat message to d-allowtest12849 -- does it succeed (confirming room-allow genuinely supports a real multi-entry list, extending write access beyond just the owner and one designated writer), or does it fail (meaning room-allow only ever recognizes a single value, and "list" is just naming, not actual multi-entry semantics)? (4) if the first format guess fails, note what error (if any) came back and, if there's any hint in the error text about the expected format, try that. Success: a decisive answer on whether room-allow genuinely supports multiple simultaneous authorized writers, or whether -- despite its name -- it only ever functions as a single designated-writer slot, closing a real, previously-untested piece of this room's authorization model.
